No projects have been accepted yet for R's participation in GSoC 2015.

Project ideas are on the new R GSoC wiki on github, proposed by mentors
or students. Some are still trickling in, as the do every year, but
most should be there.

If you have a project proposal, I suggest that you discuss it with the
maintainers of the RIGHT package. We will be very unlikely to accept a
project that has little or no chance of being accepted into the package
that is being worked on. That would be a waste of our time, and
Google's money.
> 2) Is there any mobile API for R packages?

No.

messages.author: 43b6c2f7e9e0e9b0
messages.subject: Re: RIGHT package
parts:
Dear Brent,

The key difference between shiny and RIGHT lies in whether the client or the server supports the basic interactivity, such as hovering and brushing among linked plots. Shiny, together with ggvis, supports most of the interactivity, including the basic ones, from the server side. (Shiny alone can only provide static plots.) For instance, if a graphical element is selected, the updates are made through the server-side code. RIGHT tries to support basic interactivity from the client side, your browser. This makes certain operations more responsive at the cost of implementing plotting routines in JavaScript. For more complex interactivity, RIGHT relies on shiny and server-side R code.

RIGHT still has a long way to go to become as mature as shiny or ggvis. Unfortunately, the key developers of the RIGHT package lack time to support a GSoC project this year, and we feel sorry about that.

Sincerely,
Junghoon Lee
